correctness.rationale: The finite graph is uniquely characterized and internally checked. A complete 1949-face, 970-pair acyclic Morse matching is explicitly regenerated and its 7819 directed Hasse incidences checked. The signed 5-by-3 integral Morse boundary has two primitive unit pivots and one free degree-three generator, yielding \(S^3\vee3S^4\) by CW attaching-degree theory. True 25-term degree-three and 56/98/56-term degree-four cycles are constructed and proven closed. Their exact automorphism actions yield a rank-one (-,-) module and a degree-four swapped pair plus negative line; the index-two eigensublattice follows directly.

originality.rationale: The Robertson graph is a specific canonical nontransitive nineteen-vertex cage. Relevant primary graph and independence-complex papers were inspected at theorem/section level: Engström's bounds do not compute this homotopy type; Perarnau–Perkins studies independent-set occupancy but gives no homology representation. Targeted indexed and published-record searches returned no statement implying the mixed wedge and the exact integral D12 module. Equivalent unindexed calculations remain a genuine risk; absence of results is not proof of priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis or computational topology archive may independently contain the same exact cage homotopy or lattice.
Searches cannot certify first publication priority; full access to every relevant monograph was not available.

value.rationale: The Robertson graph is the unique (4,5)-cage, a natural extremal graph studied in independence-set counting. Determining its complete mixed-dimensional homotopy type, full integral D12 representation, and the index-two parity obstruction is a coherent intrinsic classification. These invariants are not known-table recomputations, and the parity phenomenon is invisible to the ordinary homology ranks and rational character alone.
